ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a schematic diagram of a certain electromagnetic pump model. The pump body is a rectangular solid with length L1, and width and height both L2. The pump body is in a uniform magnetic field whose direction is vertically outward and whose magnetic induction intensity is B. The upper and lower surfaces of the pump body are connected to a power supply with voltage U (internal resistance neglected), and the reading of the ideal ammeter is I. If the height difference between the electromagnetic pump and the water surface is h, the resistivity of the liquid is ρ, the mass of liquid pumped in time t is m, the resistance between the liquid in flowing and the pipe wall is neglected, and the acceleration of gravity is taken as g, then
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: the kinetic energy of the liquid of mass m when leaving the pump body is $UIt-mgh-I^2\frac\rho{L_2}t$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a schematic diagram of a certain electromagnetic pump model. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a schematic diagram of an electromagnetic pump model. On the left side there are a power supply, a switch, and an ideal ammeter A connected to the pump body; the voltage U is marked between the upper and lower electrodes; the pump body is drawn as a rectangular solid, and the length L1 and transverse dimension L2 are marked; the pump body is in the magnetic field marked B; the right end is connected to a pipe extending into the water, and h represents the height difference between the pump body and the water surface. Then reason: within time t, the electrical energy input by the power supply to the electromagnetic pump is UIt. Take the pump and this section of pumped-out liquid of mass m as the energy-conversion object; the problem states that the resistance between the flowing liquid and the pipe wall is neglected, so mechanical-energy loss is not considered. One part of the electrical energy is converted into the gravitational potential energy mgh of the liquid, one part is converted into the kinetic energy K of the liquid when leaving the pump body, and another part is converted into Joule heat in the liquid resistance. Here, according to this electromagnetic-pump model, make an equivalent treatment of the ohmic loss of the conducting liquid inside the pump body, taking the equivalent resistance R=ρ/L2, so the Joule heat is I^2Rt=I^2(ρ/L2)t. By conservation of energy: UIt=mgh+K+I^2(ρ/L2)t, therefore the kinetic energy of the liquid of mass m when leaving the pump body is K=UIt-mgh-I^2ρt/L2.
